findings.expected: Per the requirement ('word ends at the first closing brace and is not recursively interpolated'), OUT == '${OTHER}' (literal word '${OTHER' plus the trailing '}'). The nested-expansion repair yields 'expanded' and is still accepted by the grader.
findings.gap: The requirement mandates a flat grammar where the alternate word ends at the first closing brace and is never recursively interpolated, but the grader's 'literal' case only checks a brace-free word ($OTHER, empty, α/β) and a malformed unterminated expression; it never puts a closing brace inside the word. Therefore a repair that adds nested-brace matching/expansion for ${...} inside the word (while still leaving bare $OTHER literal) passes every grader case yet violates the flat-grammar rule.
findings.wrong_repair: A repair that balances nested braces so that in ${BASE:+${OTHER}} the word is ${OTHER} and is recursively expanded.

answer.limitations: Reviewed only the flat/nonrecursive and literal-word aspect against the supplied packet; the full grader beyond byte 4413 and other parser files were not inspected, so other acceptance gaps may exist.

citations.quote: Add ${NAME:+word} interpolation to python-dotenv: substitute word only when NAME resolves to a nonempty string; otherwise substitute an empty string. Apply this through dotenv_values and load_dotenv, preserving override precedence between earlier file values and the process environment. Keep the existing flat expression grammar: word ends at the first closing brace and is not recursively interpolated; do not add nested expansion or shell evaluation. Preserve existing ${NAME}, ${NAME:-default}, bare variables, adjacent substitutions, interpolate=False, unassigned keys and malformed-expression behavior. Do not change unrelated parsing or environment behavior.
